context: Rebuild dbgen and qgen from _sources/tpc-h/dbgen/ with an explicit lower MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET (e.g. 15.0) or on an older runner, verify with `vtool -show` that minos <= 15.0, confirm generation still matches the reference query/data set, then re-bless benchbox/_binaries/tpc-h/darwin-arm64/checksums.md5.
description:
chatgpt-codex-connector review finding on merged PR #1256 (P2), deferred from the first PR-review sweep (PR #1259) and tracked in GitHub issue #1260.

The packaged darwin-arm64 binaries committed in #1256 were built on macOS 26 and carry LC_BUILD_VERSION minos 26.0 (verified with `vtool -show` on both qgen and dbgen; the previous packaged qgen had minos 15.0). On macOS 15.x and earlier dyld rejects a binary whose minos exceeds the host OS. Because benchbox/_binaries/tpc-h/darwin-arm64/checksums.md5 MATCHES these binaries, ensure_tpc_binaries() selects the precompiled path instead of rebuilding, so TPC-H data/query generation fails on Apple Silicon installs running macOS <= 15.
Thread: https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/pull/1256#discussion_r3626428542
Issue: https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/issues/1260

Why this was deferred from the code sweep: re-blessing a committed binary's checksum is provenance-governed (make audit-sha-check, SHA-provenance evidence tree), the rebuilt bytes depend on the local toolchain, and TPC spec-correctness of the rebuilt generator needs verification beyond a code-fix sweep.

Related open item: resync-tpch-darwin-x86-64-binaries covers the x86_64 drift; consider doing both rebuilds in one controlled session.

anti_patterns.dont: bundle this binary rebuild into an unrelated code PR
anti_patterns.instead: land it as its own PR with the vtool evidence in the body
anti_patterns.why: binary diffs are unreviewable alongside code and the provenance decision needs to be explicit

anti_patterns.dont: re-bless checksums.md5 before verifying generated output against the reference set
anti_patterns.instead: verify generation first, then update the manifest
anti_patterns.why: the checksum only pins bytes; it proves nothing about spec-correctness

preserves.behavior: TPC-H generated data and queries stay spec-correct and byte-comparable to the reference set
The EOL_HANDLING trailing-pipe framing guard still passes for the rebuilt dbgen
checksums.md5 stays in the GNU 'hash filename' format the verifier parses

work_units.summary: Rebuild darwin-arm64 dbgen + qgen with MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 and confirm `vtool -show` reports minos <= 15.0
Verify the rebuilt generators produce spec-correct output (reference query set + data framing guard) before blessing
Update benchbox/_binaries/tpc-h/darwin-arm64/checksums.md5 and confirm ensure_tpc_binaries() selects the precompiled path
